city.los-angeles.tagline: Sunset sessions, label money and a studio on every corner.
city.los-angeles.edge_why: Label lunches teach you how a rate card really works.
city.los-angeles.blurb: The studio capital of the Pacific: every second building has a live room and a story about who cut what there.
city.los-angeles.legend: They say a producer in LA is only ever one lunch away from a hit, or a very long wait for the check.
city.los-angeles.landmark_1: A Hollywood tracking floor with a famous echo chamber
city.los-angeles.landmark_2: A canyon house with a mountain of tape
city.los-angeles.era_analog60s: Session players, tiki bars and big-band engineers hand the town its first sound.
city.los-angeles.era_digital80s: Gloss, gated drums and a label on every corner.
city.los-angeles.era_internet2000s: Every bedroom is a studio; the boulevards still pay for the polish.
city.los-angeles.era_streaming2020s: Streaming money, beat-makers in rented villas and one very good taco truck.
city.nashville.tagline: Songwriters on every porch and a round at every bar.
city.nashville.edge_why: Writers' rounds sharpen your ear for a hook that holds.
city.nashville.blurb: Music City: songwriters share stages the way other towns share parking lots, and a three-chord idea is a serious thing.
city.nashville.legend: Locals swear the best songs are written between the first coffee and the second verse.
city.nashville.landmark_1: A radio-station-turned-studio with a beloved vocal booth
city.nashville.landmark_2: A honky-tonk with a stage-door demo tape box
city.nashville.era_analog60s: Country meets rock and roll in tiny rooms with big, warm microphones.
city.nashville.era_digital80s: Polished Nashville pop-country finds its crossover audience.
city.nashville.era_internet2000s: Writers sell songs to every genre; the town learns to wear a different hat.
city.nashville.era_streaming2020s: Indie-folk and streaming playlists put the old rooms back on the map.
city.london.tagline: Pirate radio, Soho studios and a taste for whatever is next.
city.london.edge_why: Short sessions and tight budgets teach you to hold focus.
city.london.blurb: Basement studios, pirate aerials and a music press that decides what is cool by Tuesday.
city.london.legend: Every London engineer has a recording ruined by the Northern line, and a tale that makes up for it.
city.london.landmark_0: A Soho basement with a ceiling pipe that sings
city.london.landmark_2: A railway-arch room with train-timed takes
city.london.era_analog60s: The Mod beat boom and the first real British studio sound.
city.london.era_digital80s: Synth-pop, post-punk and a hundred bands in one postcode.
city.london.era_internet2000s: Britpop, garage and dance floors that never really close.
city.london.era_streaming2020s: Grime, bedroom pop and big-label rooms turned into co-working desks.
city.berlin.tagline: Club culture, cheap rent and rooms that never close.
city.berlin.edge_why: Warehouse rigs and modular racks make you fluent in signal flow.
city.berlin.blurb: Concrete, club culture and the cheap rent that lets weird ideas run all night.
city.berlin.legend: They say Berlin doesn't close; it just changes tempo around six a.m.
city.berlin.landmark_1: A hall by the Wall with a famous drum room
city.berlin.landmark_2: A Kreuzberg backroom with a modular wall
city.berlin.era_analog60s: A divided city, a cold-war sound and a few studios by the border.
city.berlin.era_digital80s: Krautrock's children meet synth pop in a half-empty city.
city.berlin.era_internet2000s: Reunified rooms, techno clubs and rent so low the experiments never stop.
city.berlin.era_streaming2020s: A global capital of electronic music, with a waiting list for the good rooms.
city.tokyo.tagline: Immaculate rooms, vinyl bars and pop built like precision gear.
city.tokyo.scene: Shibuya live houses and vinyl bars
city.tokyo.edge_why: A culture of immaculate craft rewards every careful detail.
city.tokyo.blurb: Immaculate rooms, vinyl bars the size of a closet and pop engineered like fine hardware.
city.tokyo.legend: A veteran engineer here can tell a patch cable was bought secondhand just by the way it sounds.
city.tokyo.landmark_0: A Shibuya live house with a perfect small room
city.tokyo.landmark_1: A vinyl listening bar under a railway arch
city.tokyo.landmark_2: A Roppongi tower studio with a city-wide view
city.tokyo.era_analog60s: Jazz kissas and mellow ballads; the first big studios open their doors.
city.tokyo.era_digital80s: City pop, synthesizers and the world's best-built hardware.
city.tokyo.era_internet2000s: Idol factories, J-pop hits and rooms packed with gear.
city.tokyo.era_streaming2020s: Streaming brings city pop back; the vinyl bars are full again.
city.rio.tagline: Samba schools, funk parties and music that lives outdoors.
city.rio.edge_why: Samba schools teach you where the one really is.
city.rio.blurb: Samba schools, funk parties and music that lives outdoors, and a room that fits ninety drummers is called intimate.
city.rio.legend: Local engineers say the secret of any Rio record is simple: leave the door open and let the street in.
city.rio.landmark_0: A Lapa roda de samba room with a famous hum
city.rio.landmark_1: A hillside favela studio with a rooftop live room
city.rio.landmark_2: A Copacabana bossa-nova apartment with a legendary piano
city.rio.era_analog60s: Bossa nova turns apartments into studios and exports a whole mood.
city.rio.era_digital80s: Tropicalia's children meet synthesizers and a very loud pop scene.
city.rio.era_internet2000s: Baile funk and electronic crossovers pour out of the hills.
city.rio.era_streaming2020s: Streaming turns local funk into a global party playlist.
city.detroit.tagline: Assembly-line rhythm, basement techno and records built to move.
city.detroit.scene: West Grand Boulevard and basement machines
city.detroit.edge_why: Detroit sessions teach every player to serve the groove.
city.detroit.blurb: A factory town that treated the studio like an instrument: tight rhythm sections upstairs, futuristic machines below street level.
city.detroit.legend: Detroit engineers say a record is ready when the line moves, the bass holds and nobody wastes a note.
city.detroit.landmark_0: A converted house with a crowded attic echo chamber
city.detroit.landmark_1: A downtown ballroom where the floor adds its own backbeat
city.detroit.landmark_2: A basement room wired for drum machines after midnight
city.detroit.era_analog60s: House bands, handclaps and an assembly-line studio turn soul records into a worldwide sound.
city.detroit.era_digital80s: Synths and drum machines carry the city pulse from basement parties to dance floors.
city.detroit.era_internet2000s: Hip-hop, garage rock and independent rooms rebuild around the city’s stubborn musical core.
city.detroit.era_streaming2020s: Producers connect soul history, techno precision and rap sessions across a renewed studio network.
city.lagos.tagline: Highlife guitars, restless grooves and a city louder than the monitors.
city.lagos.edge_why: Long band sets teach you when a groove is about to turn.
city.lagos.blurb: A coastal megacity where highlife, Afrobeat, gospel and pop meet traffic, generators and audiences that expect the band to play on.
city.lagos.legend: The city’s producers say the best take begins after the arrangement has outgrown the page.
city.lagos.landmark_0: A Surulere room built around a broad live floor
city.lagos.landmark_1: A hotel bandstand where arrangements grow overnight
city.lagos.landmark_2: An island studio whose generator has perfect timing
city.lagos.era_analog60s: Highlife bands fill hotel rooms and radio studios with guitars, horns and dance-floor arrangements.
city.lagos.era_digital80s: Afrobeat’s long forms meet boogie keyboards, cassette studios and a fast-moving pop circuit.
city.lagos.era_internet2000s: Home studios and music-video channels carry a new Nigerian pop sound across the continent.
city.lagos.era_streaming2020s: Afrobeats sessions travel worldwide while Lagos rooms keep the percussion and call-and-response close.
gear.why.label: Why does a pro reach for this?
gear.why.compressor: A compressor evens out loud and quiet moments, so a vocal or drum sits steady in the mix instead of jumping out and vanishing.
gear.why.preamp: A preamp lifts a tiny mic signal to a usable level. Set it hot enough to beat noise, but not so hot that it clips, and its tone colors everything after it.
gear.why.reverb: Reverb places a sound in a space. A little makes a dry take feel real; a lot pushes it back behind everything else.
gear.why.microphone: Where you place a mic changes the sound more than the mic itself. Closer is fuller and drier, farther is airier and roomier.
gear.why.monitor: Monitors are your reference. You can only fix what you can hear, and a flat, honest speaker keeps mixes translating to other systems.
gear.why.interface: An interface turns analog signal into digital. Healthy gain here keeps takes clean: low enough to avoid clipping, high enough to stay above the noise.
gear.why.outboard: Outboard gear shapes tone and dynamics with hardware character. Pros reach for it to add color and control before the mix gets crowded.
gear.why.recorder: The recorder is where the signal is captured. Knowing the path into it helps you find where noise or loss creeps in.
gear.why.mixer: A mixer blends many sources and sets their levels. Gain staging channel by channel keeps the whole path clean.
chain.learn.microphone: The mic is first in the chain for a reason: nothing downstream can add detail it never heard, so the capsule and its placement set the ceiling.
chain.learn.preamp: The preamp comes right after the mic because a mic signal is tiny. Lifting it early keeps it well above the noise of every later stage.
chain.learn.dynamics: Compression after the preamp tames peaks once the signal is healthy, so the recorder is not hit by sudden spikes and the vocal stays even.
chain.learn.recorderInterface: The recorder comes last: it prints whatever arrives. Leave a little headroom so a loud take never clips.
gear.effects.none: Starter kit: no quality or speed change, it just gets you recording.
